candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Find a least common denominator (LCD) and rewrite one or both fractions as equivalent fractions with that denominator before subtracting.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts use the same skill name and essentially identical definition focused on finding an LCD/LCM and converting to equivalent fractions with a shared denominator.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract once quantities are in compatible form (same denominator and/or separated whole and fractional parts) by subtracting numerators and/or whole-number parts and combining the result.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A:S02, B:S02, and C:S02 all describe executing the subtraction after alignment (like denominators or separated whole/fraction parts) and combining into a single result.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Regroup by borrowing 1 from the whole-number part (or rewriting a whole as a mixed form) to make the fractional subtraction nonnegative, then continue the subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A:S03 and B:S03 explicitly include borrowing 1 whole into fractional units to avoid a negative fractional subtraction; C isolates this same borrowing/regrouping operation as S04.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce fractions (including zero fractions) to lowest terms and express the final value in simplest acceptable form (integer, proper/improper fraction, or mixed number).
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A:S04 and B:S04 are dedicated simplification skills; C combines rewriting and simplification in S03, but its inclusion criteria explicitly cover reducing fractions and simplifying to integers, matching this concept.

alignment_summary: Across the three codebooks, four distinct concepts cover the full workflow: (1) converting to a common denominator, (2) performing the subtraction once aligned, (3) borrowing/regrouping from the whole part when needed, and (4) simplifying the result. Expert C splits borrowing into its own skill (S04) but merges simplification with other rewriting actions (S03), which aligns most directly with the simplify-to-lowest-terms concept used by A and B.
